problem: Social navigation methods (human-model-based DRL, imitation learning, direct VLM querying) ignore social/environment context, cannot adapt online, or are too slow. Instance image-goal navigation (IIN) methods fail on goal images from arbitrary viewpoints, and 3DGS-based methods need a pre-built dense map.
motivation: Robots in human-centered spaces must reason about social and visual/semantic context to navigate safely among people and to find specific objects or people. Real deployments involve unseen social scenarios, unknown environments and goal images taken from arbitrary viewpoints.
key_idea: Two context-aware architectures: OLiVia-Nav distills a large VLM's social reasoning into lightweight CLIP-style encoders that support online lifelong learning, and SplatSearch builds a sparse online 3DGS map, renders novel views around candidate objects, inpaints them with multi-view diffusion, and matches them to the goal image.
insight: Distilling a VLM into small encoders keeps social reasoning at about 5 Hz, versus 0.6 Hz for direct GPT-4o querying, which causes longer personal-space violations. In SplatSearch, ablations show novel-view rendering and diffusion inpainting both matter: removing NVSM drops HM3D-val SR from 0.6983 to 0.3409, and removing VCICN drops it to 0.5380. Building the map online, rather than pre-building it as GaussNav does, gives much better SPL (0.3038 vs 0.0589).
method: SC-CLIP: a distillation process that trains a ViT-L/14 image encoder and a transformer text encoder, using Long-CLIP-style loss, to align RGB images with GPT-4o long and short social-context captions (20k images from MuSoHu).
Lifelong Learning Updater: buffers images, labels them with GPT-4o, and fine-tunes both encoders online with a symmetric image-text contrastive loss.

Trajectory Planning Network: LiDAR voxel encoder, goal encoder and SC-CLIP embedding fused by three sequential cross-attention layers, then GRU heads predict K=5 trajectories, trained with winner-takes-all loss on MuSoHu expert trajectories.
Trajectory Selection Module + PID controller: selects the trajectory matching the high-level action in the retrieved text embedding, then tracks it with a PID controller.
Map Generation Module: incremental sparse 3DGS map from RGB-D and odometry, plus a BLIP-2 cosine-similarity value map with a confidence-weighted update for frontier scoring.
SOIM + NVSM: YOLOv7 with MobileSAM detects and localizes goal-class objects in the 3DGS map, then N_R viewpoints are rendered on an upper hemisphere around each object centroid.

VCICN + FEM: a multi-view diffusion inpainting network (16 views collected, trained with 12 frames) completes the rendered views, then EfficientLoFTR match counts against the goal image give an object score.
Exploration Planner: picks frontiers by maximizing a weighted sum of inverse distance, object score and value map, then navigates with the Fast Marching Method.

setting.backbone: OLiVia-Nav: SC-CLIP (ViT-L/14 + transformer text encoder) + TPN + TSM, trained from scratch, with GPT-4o as the teacher VLM. SplatSearch: 3DGS + YOLOv7/MobileSAM + BLIP-2 + trained multi-view diffusion inpainter + EfficientLoFTR.
setting.training_data: OLiVia-Nav: MuSoHu, 20k images with GPT-4o captions, 5k expert trajectories, 20k selection samples. SplatSearch: about 20k objects x 16 sparse views collected by running the pipeline on the 145 HM3DSem-v0.2 training scenes.
setting.observation: OLiVia-Nav: RGB + 3D LiDAR. SplatSearch: egocentric RGB-D + odometry.
setting.action_space: OLiVia-Nav: predicted trajectories tracked by a PID controller giving linear and angular velocity. SplatSearch: frontier goals executed with FMM path planning.
setting.simulator: Habitat (HM3DSem-v0.2) for SplatSearch; OLiVia-Nav evaluated on the real world and on MuSoHu hold-out data.
setting.privileged: none stated (SplatSearch uses odometry/pose; goal class comes from the goal image)

results: SplatSearch reaches SR/SPL of 0.6983/0.3038 on HM3D-val and 0.6639/0.2703 on HM3D-val-hard, beating GaussNav (0.6492/0.0589 and 0.5828/0.0398), UniGoal and IEVE. OLiVia-Nav has the lowest MSE, Hausdorff and PSV in all four real-world social scenarios versus VLM-Social-Nav and MultiSoc, running at about 5 Hz versus 0.6 Hz for VLM-Social-Nav.
limitations: OLiVia-Nav modules are trained independently, and it ignores gestures and speech.
SplatSearch's 3DGS memory grows with scene size, and the pipeline fails if the object detector (SOIM) misses the goal class.
The social navigation evaluation is small (3 trials per scenario), and only two baselines are compared.
